resources.string: The two sides are identical as far as this comparison can see.
Only part of the result is compared: A has %1$d rows, B has %2$d rows.
The two sides did not run the same query, so a difference may come from the query rather than the data.
Pick the columns that identify a row, for example id. Rows are then matched across the two sides and a changed row shows which cells moved.
Not compared: the key %1$s is not unique %2$s — %3$d rows share the value %4$s.
Not compared: the key %1$s is NULL in %3$d rows %2$s, and NULL does not identify a row.
Not compared: the key column(s) %1$s are not in both results.
Rows are never paired on a key that repeats, because the counts would be guesses. Choose other columns, or narrow the query.
The columns have the same names but not in the same order or number.
